phase3_findings.description: _trim_unanswered_tool_use discards truncate_messages' boolean return and logs 'removed N message(s)' at WARNING even when the store removed nothing; the unanswered tool_use stays and the next call is rejected, while _rollback_conversation checks the same return value.
No test covers _tool_use_ids' provider_content branch (tool_use blocks with empty tool_calls), which criterion 2 names.
_RaisingReadStore fails from the third get_conversation read, coupling the test to the vendored agent's read count.

The diff-added _trim_unanswered_tool_use docstring claims it 'Never raises Exception' with read, lookup and call guarded, but the scan at line 295 (_first_unanswered_tool_use / _tool_use_ids) is unguarded and can raise on a malformed stored message; checklist VC-8 confirms.
_tool_use_ids is declared set[str] but line 237 can add None for a tool_use block with no id.
A malformed tool_use block with no id adds None to the id set silently; the trim fails safe but records nothing.
Baseline state is three loose locals (baseline_user, baseline_messages, queued_id) with the same two-part check repeated at lines 595, 600 and 611.
The trim's catch-all over truncate_messages does not distinguish ConversationOwnerMismatchError from a store fault, unlike _rollback_conversation.

report:
## Verdict: REJECT (a Critical silent-failure finding and a self-contradicting docstring the diff added)

This PR is not ready to merge: when the store removes nothing, the new trim still logs that it removed messages, and the new trim helper's docstring promises it never raises when part of its work runs outside any guard.
Rule applied: self-contradicting-diff carve-out; rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold (Critical) → REJECT also matches.

## Code Review Findings

### 🔴 Critical

1. In `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 310-327, `_trim_unanswered_tool_use` calls `truncate(conversation_id, user.id, cut)` and throws away the boolean it returns. `BoundedConversationStore.truncate_messages` returns `False` when it removes nothing, for example for an evicted or unknown conversation id. The trim then still logs at WARNING "removed %d message(s) from its history", using a count it computed before the call. So the unanswered `tool_use` stays in the history, the next call on this conversation is rejected by the model API, and the only log line says the history was repaired. The sibling `_rollback_conversation` in the same file checks the same return value (`rolled_back = truncate(...)`) and branches on it. (raised by 1/6 agents)

### 🟠 Important / Major

- VC-8: FAIL (important) — The trim never raises Exception: the read, the method lookup and the call are each guarded. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:276]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  query_database.py:276-280 docstring says _trim_unanswered_tool_use 'Never raises Exception' and that the caller's result must not be replaced by a cleanup failure. Only get_conversation (282-292) and truncate (310-321) are in try/except. Line 295 `_first_unanswered_tool_use(conversation.messages, start)` is unguarded, and it runs _tool_use_ids (227-238). Message.provider_content is typed Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] (agent/core/llm/models.py:26), so a schema-valid stored block {"type":"tool_use","id":["x"]} reaches `ids.add(block.get("id"))` at line 237 and raises TypeError (unhashable). A custom conversation store returning malformed messages (missing .role etc.) would also raise from lines 249-258. The exception propagates out of the trim, contradicting the absolute claim. Realistic Anthropic ids are strings, so reach is narrow, but the claim is absolute and the scan is outside any guard.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor

1. In `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 227-239, no test covers the `provider_content` branch of `_tool_use_ids`, where an assistant message carries `tool_use` blocks while `tool_calls` is empty. Acceptance criterion 2 names this source. Every test in `tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py` uses messages the real agent builds, and those fill `tool_calls`, so a change that broke this loop would not fail any test. (raised by 2/6 agents)
2. In `tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py` lines 317-330, `_RaisingReadStore` fails only from the third `get_conversation` call onward (`if self.reads >= 3:`). The test assumes the baseline read and the agent's own read are exactly the first two. If the vendored agent ever reads the store once more, the failure would hit the agent instead of the trim, and the test could still pass while no longer covering the trim's guarded read. (raised by 2/6 agents)
3. In `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 276-279, the `_trim_unanswered_tool_use` docstring says it "Never raises `Exception`" because "the read, the method lookup and the call are each guarded". The scan at line 295 (`_first_unanswered_tool_use(conversation.messages, start)`, which runs `_tool_use_ids`) is not inside any `try`. A stored message of an unexpected shape, such as a `tool_use` block whose `id` is a list (unhashable at line 237), or a custom store's message with no `.role`, raises out of the helper and replaces the call's own result or error. The method lookup at line 299 is a `getattr` with a default, not a guarded block. Checklist item VC-8 confirms the same falsehood. (raised by 1/6 agents) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=not-held limb-one=not-evaluated limb-two=not-evaluated; evidence: the claim is about the helper's exception net (a guard's coverage), so it is a functional-coverage gap and is never capped -->
4. In `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 227-237, `_tool_use_ids` is declared `-> set[str]`, but line 237 runs `ids.add(block.get("id"))`, which adds `None` for a `tool_use` block with no `id`. The caller already types its set as `set[str | None]` to work around this. Behavior is safe, because a `None` id never matches a tool result and so the message is trimmed. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. In `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` line 237, a malformed `tool_use` block with no `id` adds `None` to the id set without logging. The outcome is a trim, which fails safe, but nothing records that the block was malformed. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. In `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 564-611, the baseline is held in three separate locals: `baseline_user: User | None`, `baseline_messages` and `queued_id`. The same check `baseline_user is not None and queued_id is not None` repeats at lines 595, 600 and 611. The types allow combinations that should not happen, such as a count with no user, so a future call site could check only one of the two conditions. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. In `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 310-321, the trim catches every `Exception` from `truncate_messages` in one branch. It does not tell a `ConversationOwnerMismatchError` apart from a store fault, which `_rollback_conversation` does. The error is still logged with its traceback and the store class, so this only costs diagnostic detail. (raised by 1/6 agents)

- VC-3: FAIL (suggestion) — The agent saves the assistant tool_use message before its tools run and their results after, with the tool messages directly following that assistant message. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:270]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Ordering holds: agent.py:695-701 does conversation.add_message(assistant tool_use) before the tool loop (738+), and tool messages are appended at 1042-1048 after all tools ran, in order, directly after the assistant message. But the agent does not SAVE at those points. conversation_store.update_conversation is called only at 351, 505, 526 (new-conversation/starter/workflow paths, before the user message) and 1185 (end of the whole send_message, after the loop). Between the tool_use append and the tool results there is no update_conversation call; add_message (models.py:45-48) only appends to the in-memory list. The persisted store sees the tool_use only because the built-in stores (local/storage.py:36-43, conversation_store.py:71-80) hand back the same live object; a store returning copies would not see it until the 1185 save, which a mid-tool failure skips. So the docstring's 'saves ... before its tools run and results after' is inaccurate as worded (it is an in-memory append, not a save), though the ordering it relies on is correct.

  </details>


## Run details

<details><summary>Run details</summary>

- Diff profile: has_new_types + test_relevant (not small_diff, not config_only); 3 changed files, 524 changed lines. detect_all_audit not set: the audit hints are ordinary id scans and test helpers, not a completeness audit.

- The command-shape table `.prflow/tmp/command-shapes.md` was absent. The vendored engine paths under `.prflow/vendor/` and `.devflow/vendor/` were absent, so the running plugin's engine (candidate 3) was used.
- Deferrals: not checked (the PR body has no deferred-findings block).
- Dirty-tree check: ran clean.
- Corroboration: findings 1 and 2 under Suggestion were each raised by the final-pass reviewer and the test analyzer with the same file, kind and overlapping lines.
- prior-report: none

- Checklist: 14 passed, 2 failed, 0 inconclusive
- <details><summary>✅ Passed items (14 of 16)</summary>

  - VC-1: Agent-saved assistant Message objects expose tool_calls (iterable of objects with .id, possibly None) and provider_content (list of dicts with type/id keys, possibly None); tool messages expose role=='tool' and tool_call_id. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:227]
  - VC-2: The Anthropic request builder replays an assistant message from provider_content when it has one, so its tool_use blocks reach the API even when tool_calls is empty. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:230]
  - VC-4: get_conversation returns the conversation including messages appended during the call, and truncate_messages(conversation_id, user.id, cut) drops messages from index cut onward. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:283]
  - VC-5: The stub client SimpleNamespace(messages=_Messages()) assigned to AnthropicLlmService._client matches how the service calls client.messages.create when not streaming, and returns an anthropic Message it can parse. [tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:133]
  - VC-6: Replacing agent.tool_registry.execute with a raising function makes the real Agent return an error answer (not raise) after saving the assistant tool_use, which query_database turns into AgentRunError. [tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:236]
  - VC-7: In an armed call, the baseline read and the agent's own load come first and the third get_conversation read is the trim's. [tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:326]
  - VC-9: Only messages from start (this call's baseline) are scanned, so an earlier call's history is never cut. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:273]
  - VC-10: truncate_messages has two production callers in tools/query_database.py: the cancellation handler and the unanswered-tool_use trim. [src/sqllens/conversation_store.py:103]
  - VC-11: With the real `Agent` and a `BoundedConversationStore`, a `query_database_impl_with_widgets` call on conversation C that is cancelled after the agent saved an assistant `tool_use` and before it saved the matching `tool_result` leaves C with exactly the messages it had before that call, and the next call on C sends an Anthropic request in which every `tool_use` block is directly followed by a `tool_result` block with the same id, and returns a non-error result. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py]
  - VC-12: With the real `Agent` and a `BoundedConversationStore`, a `query_database_impl_with_widgets` call on conversation C that ends without cancellation while a `tool_use` it saved has no `tool_result` leaves C cut back to just before the earliest assistant message that call saved with an unanswered `tool_use` — every message before it stays, the call's user message included — logs a WARNING naming C and the number of messages removed, and the next call on C sends an Anthropic request in which every `tool_use` block is directly followed by a `tool_result` block with the same id, and returns a non-error result. A `tool_use` counts as unanswered when its id, taken from the assistant message's `tool_calls` or from a `tool_use` block in its `provider_content`, has no `role="tool"` message directly after that assistant message. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:241]
  - VC-13: A call that ends without cancellation and saved an unanswered `tool_use` still returns the error it returns today: an `AgentRunError` with the `SQL execution error: ` prefix when the agent returned an error answer, and the same `RuntimeError`, with the same message, that it raises today when `send_message` raised. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:594]
  - VC-14: A call that ends without cancellation and saved no unanswered `tool_use` leaves C's history exactly as the call appended it: a failed call's user message stays ahead of the next call's, as `tests/unit/test_query_database_queue.py` pins. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:79-165]
  - VC-15: When a trim is needed and the conversation store has no `truncate_messages`, or reading the conversation or calling `truncate_messages` raises, the call logs at ERROR naming the store class, leaves the history as it was, and returns or raises the same result it would have without the trim. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:282]
  - VC-16: The change leaves the vendored Anthropic request builder (`_build_payload` in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py`) unchanged, so a conversation that reaches it with an unmatched `tool_use` by a path other than `query_database` is still sent as it is. [src/sqllens/agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py:144]

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With the real `Agent` and a `BoundedConversationStore`, a `query_database_impl_with_widgets` call on conversation C that is cancelled after the agent saved an assistant `tool_use` and before it saved the matching `tool_result` leaves C with exactly the messages it had before that call, and the next call on C sends an Anthropic request in which every `tool_use` block is directly followed by a `tool_result` block with the same id, and returns a non-error result.
- [ ] With the real `Agent` and a `BoundedConversationStore`, a `query_database_impl_with_widgets` call on conversation C that ends without cancellation while a `tool_use` it saved has no `tool_result` leaves C cut back to just before the earliest assistant message that call saved with an unanswered `tool_use` — every message before it stays, the call's user message included — logs a WARNING naming C and the number of messages removed, and the next call on C sends an Anthropic request in which every `tool_use` block is directly followed by a `tool_result` block with the same id, and returns a non-error result. A `tool_use` counts as unanswered when its id, taken from the assistant message's `tool_calls` or from a `tool_use` block in its `provider_content`, has no `role="tool"` message directly after that assistant message.
- [ ] A call that ends without cancellation and saved an unanswered `tool_use` still returns the error it returns today: an `AgentRunError` with the `SQL execution error: ` prefix when the agent returned an error answer, and the same `RuntimeError`, with the same message, that it raises today when `send_message` raised.
- [ ] A call that ends without cancellation and saved no unanswered `tool_use` leaves C's history exactly as the call appended it: a failed call's user message stays ahead of the next call's, as `tests/unit/test_query_database_queue.py` pins.
- [ ] When a trim is needed and the conversation store has no `truncate_messages`, or reading the conversation or calling `truncate_messages` raises, the call logs at ERROR naming the store class, leaves the history as it was, and returns or raises the same result it would have without the trim.
- [ ] The change leaves the vendored Anthropic request builder (`_build_payload` in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py`) unchanged, so a conversation that reaches it with an unmatched `tool_use` by a path other than `query_database` is still sent as it is.
